units.title: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation

questions.stem: A charge of $5.0\,\mu\text{C}$ is placed in a uniform electric field of $2.0\times10^{4}\,\text{N C}^{-1}$. What is the magnitude of the force on it?
A 5 μF capacitor is connected across a 12 V battery. How much charge is stored on its positive plate?

Two identical small spheres, each of mass 2.0 g and carrying the same charge q, hang from a common point by light insulating threads each 0.50 m long. In equilibrium the spheres are 3.0 cm apart, so the angle of each thread with the vertical is small. Taking $g = 10\,\text{m s}^{-2}$ and $k = 9\times10^{9}\,\text{N m}^2\text{C}^{-2}$, find q.
A long straight wire carries a uniform linear charge density of 2 nC m⁻¹. What is the electric field at a perpendicular distance of 6 cm from the wire?
The figure shows three equal charges +q at the corners A, B and C of an equilateral triangle of side a. What is the net electrostatic force on the charge at A? (k = 1/4πε₀)

options.label: A
options.text: √3 kq²/a², along the bisector of angle A, away from BC

options.label: B
options.text: 2kq²/a², along the bisector of angle A, away from BC

options.label: C
options.text: √3 kq²/a², along the bisector of angle A, towards BC

questions.stem: In a field-line diagram of two point charges q₁ and q₂, twelve lines leave q₁, six of them end on q₂ and the other six go off to infinity. No other lines are attached to q₂. What can be concluded?

options.label: A
options.text: q₁ is negative, q₂ is positive and |q₁| = 2|q₂|

options.label: B
options.text: both charges are positive and q₁ = 2q₂

options.label: C
options.text: q₁ is positive, q₂ is negative and |q₁| = 2|q₂|

options.label: D
options.text: q₁ is positive, q₂ is negative and |q₂| = 2|q₁|

questions.stem: In a hydrogen atom the electron and the proton are about $0.53\times10^{-10}\,\text{m}$ apart. Taking $k = 9\times10^{9}\,\text{N m}^2\text{C}^{-2}$ and $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\text{C}$, what is the magnitude of the electrostatic force between them?
A dipole of moment 3 × 10⁻⁹ C m lies along a uniform field of 2 × 10⁵ N C⁻¹. How much work is needed to turn it so that it points opposite to the field?
Electric current in a wire has a direction, yet it is treated as a scalar quantity. The correct reason is that

options.label: A
options.text: it is defined as charge per unit time, and time is a scalar

options.label: B
options.text: it can flow only along the length of a wire

options.label: C
options.text: its magnitude is the same at every point of every circuit

options.label: D
options.text: currents meeting at a junction add algebraically and do not obey the law of vector addition

In a metal wire that is not connected to any source of potential difference, the free electrons

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: are at rest because there is no electric field inside the wire

options.label: C
options.text: drift slowly in one direction, producing a small current

options.label: D
options.text: move only along the outer surface of the wire

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Electric power is transmitted over long distances at very high voltages.
Reason (R): For a given power, a higher transmission voltage means a smaller current, so the $I^2R$ loss in the transmission lines is reduced.

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

A $20\,\mu\text{F}$ capacitor is connected to an AC source whose voltage is $V = 100\sin(500\,t)$ volt, with $t$ in seconds. What is the peak value of the displacement current between its plates?
The remote control of a television set sends signals to the TV using which radiation?

Consider the Ampère–Maxwell law $\oint \vec B\cdot d\vec l = \mu_0 i_c + \mu_0\varepsilon_0\,\dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt}$. Which of the following statements are correct?

A. For steady currents and unchanging fields it reduces to Ampère's original circuital law.
B. A magnetic field can be produced in a region of empty space where no conduction current flows.
C. For a given closed loop, the value of $i_c + i_d$ depends on which surface bounded by the loop is chosen.
D. The term $\mu_0\varepsilon_0\, d\Phi_E/dt$ is essential for the existence of electromagnetic waves.
A $2.0\,\mu\text{F}$ capacitor is connected to a $220\,\text{V}$ (rms), $50\,\text{Hz}$ AC supply. What is the rms displacement current between its plates?

Assertion (A): Microwaves are used in radar systems for aircraft navigation.

Reason (R): Because of their short wavelength, microwaves can be sent out as narrow, well-directed beams that are reflected strongly by objects such as aircraft.

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.stem: A ray falls normally on one face of a glass prism of angle 30° and refractive index 1.5. The angle of deviation produced is about

Consider the following statements about reflection and refraction of a plane wave, based on the Huygens construction.
A. In reflection, the speed of the wave is the same before and after reflection.
B. In refraction, the wavelength changes in proportion to the speed of the wave.
C. In refraction, the frequency of the wave changes in the ratio of the speeds.
D. The ratio $\sin i/\sin r$ is constant for a given pair of media.
Choose the correct option.

Consider the following statements about Huygens' principle.
A. Every point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary wavelets.
B. The secondary wavelets spread out with the speed of the wave in that medium.
C. The backward envelope of the wavelets gives a wave travelling back towards the source.
D. The new wavefront is the forward envelope (common tangent) of the secondary wavelets.
Which statements are correct?

Assertion (A): The cladding of an optical fibre is made of a material whose refractive index is lower than that of the core.
Reason (R): Light travels faster in the core than in the cladding.

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.stem: In the photoelectric experiment, a photocurrent flows even when the potential of the collector plate relative to the emitter is zero. The reason is that:
